hypothesis: Replace allocation-heavy per-record aggregation with borrowed-key hash aggregation: split the three fields without collecting a Vec, keep endpoint slices in the standard randomized HashMap, allocate each endpoint once when producing the result, and sort only the unique output rows. Development evidence spans 512 and 8192 records with roughly 8 to 3554 distinct endpoints; removing allocations on repeated records should improve both sizes, while expected constant-time lookup should reduce the high-cardinality tree-comparison cost. Exact numeric, Unicode-control, line-ending and invalid-row validation is unchanged.
notes: Fresh model-authored proposal from the exported baseline development evidence. Static source inspection only; no compilation, correctness execution or benchmarks were run by this proposal author. The standard library randomized hasher is retained, so measurements include its normal seed variation and maintain its untrusted-input defenses. Risks: hash initialization and the final sort may cost more on tiny or mostly-unique inputs; the HashMap can use more peak memory than a BTreeMap. Borrowed keys do not escape this call, and output ordering remains lexicographic. No unsafe code, global state, persistent caching, input-specific answers, driver changes or dependency additions.
